html.title: Dog Vision - See How Dogs See the World | Real-time Color Simulator
html.description: See the world through your dog's eyes. Dog Vision uses your camera to simulate how dogs perceive colors - blue and yellow with no red or green.
html.heading: Dog Vision

article.heading: How dogs see color differently from humans
article.p1: Humans have trichromatic vision — our eyes contain three types of cone cells sensitive to red, green, and blue light. This allows us to perceive the full spectrum of colors.
article.p2: Dogs have dichromatic vision. They have only two types of cone cells: one sensitive to blue and one sensitive to yellow. This means dogs cannot distinguish between red and green — both colors appear as shades of yellow or gray to them.
article.p3: This is similar to red-green color blindness in humans. While dogs see fewer colors, they have superior night vision and better motion detection, which made them excellent hunters.
article.p4: Use the camera above to see a real-time simulation of how your dog perceives the world.

html.footer: Dog Vision — educational demonstration of canine color perception.
